first_impression.reaction: Googled 'average cost wedding photographer' because I wanted a number for the spreadsheet. Jumped to the FAQ first and the answer to the exact question I typed is 'there is no single honest figure'. Mildly annoying, but at least it says why instead of making up an average that tells me nothing. Kept reading because the intro promises the cost drivers and the contract side, and that part delivers. The rights section is the strongest thing here: dated, linked to the ACCC and the Copyright Act, quoted word for word, and honest that overseas suppliers are hard to chase. The planner pitch shows up three times and still says nothing about whether you take a cut.

journey.quote: There is no single honest figure, because a national average blends very different weddings.
journey.reaction: That's the question I searched for and you won't answer it. I get the logic, but I came for a ballpark. I'll go get one from another site and come back to this for the checklist.

journey.quote: Enough to cover what you actually want.
journey.reaction: That's a non-answer. Reads like a dodge, even if the rest of the reply is sensible.

journey.quote: Anything not written down should be treated as not included.
journey.reaction: Good. That's exactly how I'd treat a quote after the last vendor burned me.

journey.quote: What follows is what actually shapes a quote, what a package should spell out in writing, what tends to sit outside it, and where you stand before you sign.
journey.reaction: Clear contents. Tells me upfront this is about reading quotes, not a price table. Fair enough.

journey.quote: Ask which, and whether the figure is fixed or charged at cost afterwards.
journey.reaction: That's the question that catches people out. Fixed versus at-cost-afterwards goes straight into my comparison columns.

journey.quote: If an assistant is listed, ask whether they shoot or only carry equipment.
journey.reaction: Practical. That's the kind of padding I'd expect in a quote and wouldn't think to question.

journey.section: Extras that sit outside the headline package
journey.quote: The package price is the start of the conversation, not the end.
journey.reaction: Honest about where the catch usually is. The list underneath is the useful part.

journey.quote: In practice, it can be difficult to get a repair, replacement or refund from an overseas business, and you should ask the consumer protection agency where the business is based whether it can help.
journey.reaction: Admits a real limitation instead of pretending the ACL fixes everything abroad. That's the kind of honesty that makes me trust the rest.

journey.quote: Our destination photographer cost guide goes further into travel, accommodation and coverage abroad.
journey.reaction: Where? Every other guide in this section is linked and this one isn't. Looks unfinished.

journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: First pitch, before the rights section I actually care about. 'Payments' again. Do you take a cut from the venue or the photographer? The 'in writing' bit helps, but it doesn't answer that.

journey.quote: This is general information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Dated and clear about its limits. Exactly what I look for.

journey.section: Who owns the copyright in your wedding photos
journey.quote: The default can be changed. Under section 35(3), the operation of the commissioned-photograph rule "may be excluded or modified by agreement".
journey.reaction: Quotes the Act, links it, and tells me the catch: the contract can override the default. I checked the section, it says what you say. That's the bit I'd send to the group chat.

journey.section: How to compare quotes in writing
journey.quote: A lower headline price with fewer hours and a slower delivery date is a different product, not a saving.
journey.reaction: Agreed. This is basically my spreadsheet method written out, which is a compliment.

journey.section: How to compare quotes in writing
journey.quote: If you are weighing photography against everything else a wedding abroad involves, Wedded Concierge brings the whole plan into one place.
journey.reaction: Second pitch. Still no fee model, no word on commissions.

journey.section: Planning the rest of the picture
journey.quote: If photography is one of many suppliers you are lining up abroad, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee with you in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Better than most planner sites: at least it says there's a fee and it's agreed in writing up front. But how much, how it's calculated, and whether suppliers pay you on top? Silence. You just spent a whole article telling me to get every line in writing.

unanswered_questions: Even without a national average, is there any published range or real example for what photography costs on a wedding like ours? The Italy photographer cost guide might have it, but this page doesn't say.
Where is the destination photographer cost guide the article mentions? It isn't linked.
Does Wedded Concierge handle 'payments' by passing supplier prices through at cost, or is there a commission or mark-up from the photographer or venue? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee calculated, and what's a realistic 'From AUD' figure? (deferred business detail)
Show me a real destination wedding you've planned with the actual photography line and the total budget. (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Enough to cover what you actually want.
turn_offs_found.why: Evasive opener to a direct money question in the FAQ, the section I read first.

turn_offs_found.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: CTA lands before the rights section, the main evidence on the page, and 'payments' raises the commission question without answering it.

turn_offs_found.quote: If photography is one of many suppliers you are lining up abroad, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee with you in writing before any work begins.
turn_offs_found.why: The article demands full written transparency from photographers but the brand's own fee and commission position isn't stated at the point it asks me to enquire.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the 'Questions to ask before you book a wedding photographer' list and the seven-step quote comparison
Our Reddit thread: the copyright section quoting section 35(5), 35(7) and 35(3) with links to the Act

cta_reaction.quote: Start a conversation through Wedded Concierge, and for more planning ideas, read the Wedded Wonderland magazine.
cta_reaction.why: Solid, well-sourced article and I'll use the checklist and the copyright section. It didn't give me the number I searched for, which I can live with. But three pitches in, I still don't know what the planner costs or whether you take a cut from suppliers. 'Agrees the fee in writing' is a start, not an answer. I'd keep comparing.

top_3_changes: Soften the FAQ dodge: drop 'Enough to cover what you actually want.' and lead with the method (same written brief, compare inclusions), and point to the Italy photographer cost guide as a worked example for readers who want a real figure.
Move the first Wedded Concierge pitch out of the destination section (or after the rights section), and either link or remove the unlinked 'destination photographer cost guide' mention.

Near the closing CTA, state how the Wedded Wonderland fee works and whether supplier commissions or mark-ups apply (deferred business detail), so the brand meets the same 'get it in writing' standard the article sets for photographers.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, checked sources and claims, hunted for fees and commissions
No invented brand facts; fees, commissions and real weddings listed as deferred unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots, link notes) ignored
Reacted to the no-prices decision as written without inventing figures

open_questions.question: The destination photographer cost guide is mentioned in visible copy but has no link until N-508 goes live. Should the sentence be held back until the URL exists?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via a Google search for 'average cost wedding photographer' wanting a ballpark figure for his comparison spreadsheet.
The absence of prices and averages is a business decision; reacted to it as written and did not invent figures.
Business details (fees, commissions, real weddings) are deferred; voiced as unanswered questions only.
Link text quoted as rendered, without markdown syntax or HTML comments.
Read FAQ first, then extras, rights and the quote comparison closely; cost-factor subsections skimmed.
